verdict: Supported (for fixed-threshold level and all momentum rules)
evidence: Headline decisions 1972-07-31 to 2026-10-30 (n=652); core from 1996-12-31 (n=359). Min coverage of L1/M1-M4: 99.4%. Rows with release after decision: 0. Percentile rules (L2, L3) are defined for only 60% of headline decisions: ALFRED vintages before 1994-02 hold about 19 monthly observations, too few to calibrate a distribution without back-filling revised data.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Inflation level (low/normal/high) and momentum (falling/stable/rising) can be assigned from real-time ALFRED CPI vintages.
declared support criterion: Coverage >= 95% of decision dates in the primary window and release_ts <= decision_ts for every row.

evidence: Headline vs core, L1 level: weighted kappa 0.29 [0.03, 0.50], raw agreement 65% (n=359). M1 momentum: kappa 0.27 [0.17, 0.36]. Declared guide: lower bound >= 0.60.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Headline and core CPI give consistent level and momentum classifications.
declared support criterion: Lower 95% CI bound of weighted kappa >= 0.60 for the level rule.

evidence: Median pairwise weighted kappa across definitions: CORE level 0.399; CORE momentum 0.421; HEADLINE level 0.596; HEADLINE momentum 0.462. Declared guide: median >= 0.60. Pairwise range (headline level): 0.51 to 0.71.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Level/momentum labels are robust to reasonable rule definitions.

evidence: Real-time label differs from latest-revised label (share, 95% CI upper bound vs limit 5% level / 10% momentum). Pass: H:L1 1.7%, H:L2 1.0%, H:M1 8.0%, H:M2 4.3%, C:L1 0.8%, C:L2 1.7%, C:M1 4.2%, C:M2 2.8%, C:M4 6.4%. Fail: H:L3 4.1% (upper 6.4%), H:M3 21.0% (upper 25.8%), H:M4 19.4% (upper 23.3%), C:L3 4.2% (upper 7.2%), C:M3 10.3% (upper 15.1%). Short-horizon annualised-pace momentum (M3, M4) is the revision-sensitive family (seasonal-factor revisions).
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Real-time labels are rarely changed by later revisions.
declared support criterion: Upper 95% CI bound of the flip share <= 5% for the level rule and <= 10% for momentum.

evidence: H M1 confirm2: short spells 55%->18% (67% lower), added median delay 1.0m; H M1 hyst: short spells 55%->49% (10% lower), added median delay 0.0m; H M2 confirm2: short spells 43%->20% (55% lower), added median delay 1.0m; H M2 hyst: short spells 43%->41% (6% lower), added median delay 0.0m; C M1 confirm2: short spells 51%->16% (69% lower), added median delay 1.0m; C M1 hyst: short spells 51%->34% (33% lower), added median delay 0.0m; C M2 confirm2: short spells 30%->10% (66% lower), added median delay 1.0m; C M2 hyst: short spells 30%->10% (68% lower), added median delay 0.0m
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Raw momentum labels switch too often; persistence rules reduce short-lived reversals at an acceptable delay cost.
declared support criterion: confirm2/hyst cut short spells by >= 50% with a median added delay <= 3 months.

verdict: Supported on the declared timeliness criterion, but weak evidence of discrimination
evidence: Headline M1 raw: 19/19 ex-post turning points matched within 18 months, median delay 2.0 months from the observation month (IQR 2.0-3.0). Chance check: only 38% of all switches into the matching state fall inside a post-turning-point window that covers 28% of the time (lift 1.36); the rule changes state ~3.7 times a year, so catching every turn is expected and most switches are not turning points.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Momentum turns are detected within a useful delay.
declared support criterion: Median delay <= 6 months and >= 75% of turning points detected within 18 months.

evidence: Largest change when any one declared episode is excluded vs CI half-width: headline-vs-core kappa (L1) 0.255 vs 0.236; revision flip share (L1) 0.005 vs 0.010; transitions per year (L1) 0.153 vs 0.442. Excluding the 2020-26 episode drops headline-vs-core level kappa from 0.29 to 0.04.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Detection properties are stable across calibration scheme, sample start and inflation episodes.
declared support criterion: Metrics change by less than the bootstrap half-width when any one episode is removed.

evidence: high vs not-high: mean forward 3m excess return difference -1.6% per year (95% CI -5.6% to 2.5%); cells 263 / 386 months in 20 / 21 spells; bootstrap p 0.45, Holm-adjusted 1.00; effect size -0.20 sd.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Forward 3m Treasury excess returns are lower after high-inflation level states than otherwise.
declared support criterion: CI excludes 0, sign negative, Holm-adjusted p < 0.05.

evidence: rising - falling: mean forward 3m excess return difference 0.1% per year (95% CI -4.7% to 5.0%); cells 206 / 208 months in 55 / 54 spells; bootstrap p 0.96, Holm-adjusted 1.00; effect size 0.01 sd.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Forward 3m Treasury excess returns are lower after 'rising' than after 'falling' momentum states.

evidence: low - high: mean forward 3m excess return difference -2.9% per year (95% CI -8.8% to 3.2%); cells 75 / 263 months in 14 / 20 spells; bootstrap p 0.35, Holm-adjusted 1.00; effect size -0.36 sd.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Forward 3m excess returns differ between low and high level states.

evidence: (high,rising,tightening) - (high,falling,easing): mean forward 3m excess return difference 1.2% per year (95% CI -7.7% to 11.0%); cells 66 / 43 months in 20 / 15 spells; bootstrap p 0.81, Holm-adjusted 1.00; effect size 0.16 sd.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): High-and-rising inflation during tightening has worse forward 3m excess returns than high-but-falling inflation during easing.
declared support criterion: As E1 and each cell has >=12 months and >=3 spells.

evidence: 83 estimable secondary contrasts of 128 defined; 0 significant after Benjamini-Hochberg. E1 (high vs not-high, expected negative): 15/17 negative, 0 with 95% CI below 0 before correction. E2 (rising - falling, expected negative): 24/47 negative, 1 with CI below 0 before correction.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): The E1-E4 contrasts also hold for core CPI, other rules, other horizons (1m, 12m) and the IEF proxy.
declared support criterion: Consistent sign and CI exclusion across most combinations after BH.

verdict: Not supported as a general statement (declared metric); consistent for some of the deepest episodes
evidence: 1/16 drawdown peaks fall in a 'tightening' state (6%, exact 95% CI 0%-30%) vs 27% of all decisions; mean share of peak-to-trough decisions in tightening 21%. The tightening state is a trailing 6-month change, so peaks naturally precede it. Deepest episodes (<= -20%): 1976-12..1981-09 -39% (tightening 67% of decisions inside); 2020-08..2026-09 -29% (tightening 24% of decisions inside).
hypothesis (declared before analysis): The deep Treasury drawdowns (Table 5.1) are associated with Fed tightening cycles.
declared support criterion: Share of drawdown peaks in tightening materially exceeds the unconditional tightening share, in every sub-sample with >=3 episodes.

verdict: Partially consistent (descriptive only; not a clean separation)
evidence: Share of peak-to-trough decisions with headline L1 'high': deep (<= -10%, n=9) mean 33%, shallow (n=7) mean 14%. Deepest: 1976-12..1981-09 -39% high inside 100%; 2020-08..2026-09 -29% high inside 41%; 1986-08..1987-10 -16% high inside 36%. Shallow episodes with >= 90% of decisions in 'high': 2008-03..2008-06 (-7%).
hypothesis (declared before analysis): The two drawdowns deeper than 10% (1977-81, 2020-23) coincided with very high inflation; without a major inflation problem drawdowns were ~10% or less.
declared support criterion: Deep drawdown episodes start/run in 'high' level states, and shallow ones do not.

evidence: Real-yield / potential-growth claims are not tested in this study.
hypothesis (declared before analysis): Ex-post real returns depend on starting real yields (Fig 5.1); fair-value 10Y real yield ~ potential growth (Fig 5.2).
